quest.title: The Missing Village Keepers
quest.description: Entrusted by Isak, a resident of Aaru Village, you and Cyno begin looking for clues about the Village Keepers...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x900, Mora x36000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.title: King Deshret and the Three Magi

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Excuse me, did you happen to see where the missing scholars went?

dialogues.speaker: Kazan
dialogues.text: You mean the Village Keepers? Hmm, let me think...

dialogues.speaker: Kazan
dialogues.text: When I was eating dinner the other day, I saw one of them by the side of the road, muttering away and eating mushrooms and tree roots... They shouldn't go around eating that kind of stuff!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, okay, did you notice anything else?

dialogues.speaker: Kazan
dialogues.text: Anything else, hmm... No, I think that's all I have to tell you, sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The scholars that have gone missing, have you seen them?

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Whaaa! Those eyes, those fierce eyes! Y—You look like a real fighter...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Don't change the subject.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: R—Right! You were asking about the Vil— I mean, the mad scholars. I think it's been a few days since I last saw them? I usually go to bed pretty early, so I'm not too familiar with what goes on at night.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: But honestly, I feel quite sympathetic towards them. Even though they act a little strange, they've helped me in the past. If it weren't for them, my house would've collapsed long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Do you also think Grandpa and the others are good people?

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Grandpa? Oh, hello there, it's little Isak! You mean that nice man who looks like your grandpa's long-lost twin, right?

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Haha, he was actually the one who protected my house! I saw it with my own eyes. He happened to be staying near my house that day and was doing something with his hands on the ground.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: It still feels pretty surreal now that I think back on it... Did someone teach them how to do that?

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Well, whatever the case, I'll always be thankful to him and whoever taught him to look out for others. I'm pretty sure that if I ever went mad, I wouldn't be able to do anything like that...

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Gotcha! Thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Sir, have you seen my grandpa recently? You know, the one who likes to sit and space out near the village entrance...

dialogues.speaker: Jabari
dialogues.text: Oh, well if it isn't Isak! Your grandpa, huh? Hmm... it's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Jabari
dialogues.text: The last time I saw him, he was spacing out by the road as usual. I went and asked him if he'd like any of the food I had prepared, despite my wife's protests. Like many people, she's really quite terrified of them...

dialogues.speaker: Jabari
dialogues.text: *sigh* And speaking of my wife, she's still always complaining about how I don't make enough Mora... That might explain why she's always mad at me...

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Oh, thank you... Thank you for taking care of him.

dialogues.speaker: Jabari
dialogues.text: Haha, it was nothing! You're looking for him, right? Did he go for a walk and get lost?

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Yeah...

dialogues.speaker: Jabari
dialogues.text: Oof, that's no good... Well, once you've found him, come by my place again and I'll cook a little something for the both of you.

dialogues.speaker: Jabari
dialogues.text: I've known you since you were very young, so as far as I'm concerned, you're family. Please feel free to come by anytime.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, what a nice guy...

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Okay, thank you, sir.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm? What's wrong, Cyno? Did something happen?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Don't say anything for now.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hmm... Isak, stay here.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Let's head over there. Stay quiet as you move.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Listen, see if you can make out what they're saying.

dialogues.speaker: Sharkan
dialogues.text: Have you heard? The mighty King Deshret, the sovereign of our faith, will soon return to this world!

dialogues.speaker: Makan
dialogues.text: Yes, of course I have. King Deshret is the one and only true ruler of this land. I've never believed in any other gods!

dialogues.speaker: Makan
dialogues.text: Still, you say he's coming back, but... it sure doesn't feel like life's about to change around here anytime soon. What's your proof?

dialogues.speaker: Sharkan
dialogues.text: Haven't you noticed? The village has been getting more deranged scholars than ever!

dialogues.speaker: Sharkan
dialogues.text: Delavar was saying that many people also went insane just before the fall of King Deshret's civilization in ancient times. We don't quite know why, but it seems like there's some sort of a connection between insanity and King Deshret.

dialogues.speaker: Sharkan
dialogues.text: Isn't it a sign of King Deshret's power that all the mad scholars have disappeared? If you ask me, they must have been chosen as the final sacrifice for King Deshret's resurrection!

dialogues.speaker: Makan
dialogues.text: Huh, now that you say it, that does make some sense! Haha, does this mean our lives are finally going to take a turn for the better?

dialogues.speaker: Sharkan
dialogues.text: Exactly! Those city folks will get what's coming to them!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Now, repeat everything you've just said from the very beginning.

dialogues.speaker: Sharkan
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Makan
dialogues.text: Wh—Who are you!? Where did you come from?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: My patience is running thin. You heard what I asked.

dialogues.speaker: Sharkan
dialogues.text: Ah! B—Bro, this guy's something else. Just look at his eyes... One wrong move and he's gonna flay us alive...

dialogues.speaker: Makan
dialogues.text: Let's not get on his bad side, okay? I'm no match for this guy...

dialogues.speaker: Sharkan
dialogues.text: O—Okay, good sir, wh—what is it you would like to know?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Tell me about King Deshret's resurrection.

dialogues.speaker: Sharkan
dialogues.text: Well, I... I only know a few things from hearsay. I went for a drink the other day, and heard others talking about a rumor that the madmen will disappear, and that King Deshret will return to this land. I'm not making this up, I swear...

dialogues.speaker: Makan
dialogues.text: Hey, go on, keep talking!

dialogues.speaker: Sharkan
dialogues.text: It's true, it's all true, sir! We desert folk have had more than enough of those people at the Akademiya... They keep sending us all their mad scholars and won't let us have a good life...

dialogues.speaker: Sharkan
dialogues.text: Would you want to live like this if you were in our place? The Radicals were even more thrilled than me when they heard the news... We're all praying for King Deshret's speedy return.

dialogues.speaker: Sharkan
dialogues.text: Delavar also said that once King Deshret returns to our side, it's only a matter of time before we conquer the land on the other side of the Wall. They're all willing to serve under King Deshret and fight for a share of the glory...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Is that so...

dialogues.speaker: Makan
dialogues.text: Uh, seems like he still wants to know more, keep talking!

dialogues.speaker: Sharkan
dialogues.text: Ah, g—got it! I uh... at first, I told myself it was just the drink talking. But then, all the mad scholars vanished without a trace... just as the rumors said!

dialogues.speaker: Sharkan
dialogues.text: P—Please don't beat me up just for mentioning these rumors! I—If I'm guilty, then everyone else around here is also guilty! I'm just saying what the others said!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The people here really like King Deshret, but dislike the Dendro Archon...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Akademiya is probably the true target of their hatred.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Where is this "radical" person you talked about?

dialogues.speaker: Sharkan
dialogues.text: I haven't run into him over the past few days, so he probably hasn't been around the village... What about you, man — have you seen him at all?

dialogues.speaker: Makan
dialogues.text: Uh, no, not at all! We wouldn't dare lie to you. He's really not here right now!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Sounds like you're not too close with the Radicals.

dialogues.speaker: Makan
dialogues.text: No, of course not! All we know are their names.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I have many ways to stop you from talking, and many others to stop you from sending warning messages.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: So you'd best just stay home and hope I don't hear of you trying to contact anybody.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Don't do anything until I've gotten to the bottom of this. Try something foolish, and even Candace won't be able to protect you.

dialogues.speaker: Sharkan
dialogues.text: Yes, yes, got it! We'll do just as you say!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, that scared Paimon half to death! Cyno is pretty terrifying...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good thing I'm not one of your enemies.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Mhm.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He didn't try to reassure us at all... It's like he's used to hearing that. Paimon bets lots of people have told him that before...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All the more reason for you to not get on his bad side...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I heard that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahh, sorry!!!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It's part of being a matra.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The rumor we heard just now seems like a strong lead. But we need to check a few more places.

choices.text: Maybe we could check the scholars' homes?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Very well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Isak!

response.speaker: Isak
response.text: Ah, I'm here!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Where's your grandpa's house?

response.speaker: Isak
response.text: I can take you there. Just follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: This is where Grandpa usually stays.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There sure isn't much here...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hm? What's that smell...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Cyno, did you catch a faint whiff of incense?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: No.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Incense? Ahh! Please don't say it's that same one as before!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's definitely that one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But are you okay!? Are you getting dizzy or need to lie down?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: There's a scent that you can sense, but I can't...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A certain Traveler here once passed out from that smell. Thankfully, Tighnari saved the day... and then he gave us a long lecture to explain all about how it worked...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...So you know Tighnari.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You know him too? Are you two friends?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Hmm, now that I concentrate, I can also make out the scent of incense.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Wait, surely Tighnari didn't lecture you, too?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: No. No need.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can't handle this scent very well...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Did you first encounter this scent at Tighnari's house?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No, it was in the forest where a scholar was meditating.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: In the forest... from a scholar...

choices.text: Let's keep looking for more clues.
It'd be more efficient if we split up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you looking for, Cyno?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Here it is.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Take a look right here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Erm... Paimon doesn't see anything.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Although the traces have been completely buried in the sand, there are footprints here.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: From the size and shape, they belong to an adult male. This pattern is a common one from this area. Local shoes... This was probably someone from the village.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The scent is quite faint... but still extant. The footprints head in that direction.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You mean someone else has been here?

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: But who would come looking for Grandpa? He doesn't have any friends.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We'd have to ask whoever lured him away with the incense.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Lured him away... So that's what happened!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So you can lure someone away with just a scent?

choices.text: You get lured away by food all the time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, what's wrong with liking good food!? Everyone's got something they love in life!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Exactly. Most scholars are fond of incense, since the smell supposedly helps them clear their minds and discover new knowledge.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Even deep within the clutches of madness, they still yearn for their knowledge-seeking days, and will follow the scent whenever it presents itself.

response.speaker: Isak
response.text: No... Grandpa...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So someone's taking advantage of their weakness, huh... Still, why would anyone wanna abduct all the scholars?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is it to resurrect King Deshret?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are the rumors really true?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's the only lead we have so far.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Could the disappearance of all the mad scholars have something to do with the Radicals?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: It's highly likely.

response.speaker: Isak
response.text: Please, you have to save my grandpa! Grandpa's never done anything wrong. Please help him!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like we'd better help get him back! Don't you worry, Isak, we won't let whoever took him get away with it!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Let's head to Aaru Village and inform Candace and the others about what we learned here. After that, we'll set off to find the scholars.

choices.text: You fall for that kind of thing all the time, Paimon.

talks.objective: Go back to the village chief's house

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: ...Right, the dark fabric definitely looks a lot better. That'd be my choice, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back, Candace! We've got a lot to tell you!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Ah, welcome back!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Heh, sounds like everyone's friends already.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Dehya's here too!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You bet! So, everything go smoothly?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Reasonably.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hmm? Alhaitham didn't go with you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We haven't seen him at all!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Huh, I saw him around the village entrance earlier and figured he was investigating with you... I guess he must have gone off on his own.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Did you find out anything useful?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Candace and Dehya everything you've learned...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I see. So, someone used a kind of incense to lead the exiled scholars away from the village...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: The resurrection of King Deshret? First I've heard of it...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Far as I know, the kind of incense you just mentioned is only popular beyond the wall.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Scholars are fond of it, but as you can see, there aren't many scholars still studying around these parts. No seller would be able to make a profit here.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Not to mention, making incense is a labor-intensive process. You won't see anybody in the desert with the patience to make or sell something that requires that kind of effort.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: It seems someone from beyond the wall must have been supporting this.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Makes sense.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, so what should we do then? Do we go back to the Akademiya and search for leads there?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: If it was any other day, that would be your next logical step. But today, you've got me on your team, so you get an extra tip.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Didn't you say that the villager got his news from the tavern? Well, I also like to drink at the tavern, so I know a thing or two about these radicals he mentioned.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If Paimon remembers correctly, the leader of the Radicals is some guy called Delavar!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Ah yeah, Delavar the "Scar-Riddled Bandit," Engur the "Wide-Eyed Butcher," and Jabari the "Ducktail-Bearded Crook." The whole lot of 'em are known around these parts.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I feel like I've heard these names somewhere before...)

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: These guys have one thing in common, and that's being broke. The rougher life gets, the more they wanna believe in King Deshret. Way they see it, King Deshret's resurrection is their only chance at overthrowing the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Throwing all of Sumeru into chaos is the only way to change the way of life here in the desert. Anyway, that's my guess why they've chosen to become radicals.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dehya, you're amazing! You really know this place inside and out!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But Dehya, I...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Huh? Dehya's winking at me... Maybe I should stay quiet for now?)

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hahaha, no merc can afford to slack off on gathering intelligence! Every Mora I've spent in the tavern has been a valuable investment.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Let's head out.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Now hold on. You're staying right here, Cyno.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Why?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Aaru Village is not a big place. Outsiders stand out here like a sore thumb. I'd bet word about you has already gotten out.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: The desert is unforgiving, so the way of life here is also a lot tougher than on the other side of the wall. You survive on making connections out here.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Compared to you, mercs like me are just third-rate amateurs... I've got no actual fighting skills to speak of. But that also makes it a whole lot easier for me to gain the locals' trust.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I need to go around and ask some questions, but it'll be difficult if you're with me.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Fine.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Good, then we've got a plan. The Traveler and Paimon will go to Caravan Ribat with me, and we'll try our best to figure out where the mad scholars have been taken. Cyno, you'll have to stay in the village and continue investigating on your own.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, sounds like a plan!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, here we are again.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Sounds like you're starting to get familiar with the area.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's amazed every time we see the Wall of Samiel. How can a wall this tall even exist? It's almost... unreal.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I know what you mean. I had the same question every time I walked this way when I was a kid.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Also, why is this high wall here? And can a wall really block sandstorms?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: It was only after I grew up that I realized... the Wall of Samiel isn't just there to keep out the sandstorms. It serves a more important purpose — keeping out people like us.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Sumeru is run by wise and mighty sages. To them, us desert-dwellers are nothing but tools that can be used and discarded at their whim.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: We're cheap labor. Like livestock, but easier to control... Nothing more.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Even if a child from the desert got the chance to obtain an Akasha Terminal, almost all their requests for knowledge would be denied. The Akademiya believes we're undeserving.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Geniuses like Setaria are one in a million. The other children never get a single chance to try and rewrite their fate... Even though the Akademiya knows very well that we're humans, just as they are.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's terrible...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I would tear down this wall with my own hands if I could.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey Dehya, uh, you're not thinking about doing anything scary, are you?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Uh, no, not at all. This place just... gets me thinking, that's all.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Besides, we're here to procure information, aren't we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep! We gotta catch those—

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Shhh!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Caravan Ribat is crawling with people, so be careful what you say. We don't want anyone to find out what we're here for.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Our mission started the moment we arrived here.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Let's go check out the tavern. Maybe we'll find someone I know.

choices.text: (But I hope she doesn't do anything drastic here...)

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Just our luck... None of them are here today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean, you don't see anyone you know?
Dehya, is that you? Haha, what a coincidence! You're here for a drink, too?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hmm, Zaki? Finally, a friendly face!

dialogues.speaker: Zaki
dialogues.text: Oh? And who do you have with you here? Guests from another land?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello, nice to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Zaki
dialogues.text: Hello, hello! I'm Zaki, Dehya's... How would you put it? Drinking buddy?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Haha, we've had drinks together a few times. You could say we go back a ways.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Anyway, as far as my friends here, they aren't too shabby, are they? You rarely see any outlanders so friendly and respectful nowadays.

dialogues.speaker: Zaki
dialogues.text: Absolutely, much better than those people on the other side of the wall. So, Dehya, are you looking for someone?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Yeah, have you seen Engur, Delavar, or Jabari recently?

dialogues.speaker: Zaki
dialogues.text: Of course I have. Matter of fact, we were all here drinking together just a few days ago.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I've got a spice-trading deal from another nation... I thought maybe Delavar and his friends might be interested. Know where I could find him?

dialogues.speaker: Zaki
dialogues.text: Ah, how thoughtful of you. Then I assume you also know that Delavar's been having a hard time making ends meet these days. So, you came here to help him out?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hey, keep it down. Let's just say I'd prefer to keep this deal a secret. Y'all at Caravan Ribat are like family. If there's Mora to be made, why not do it together? Besides, Delavar and his friends have muscle. They'd be a good fit for escorting the goods.

dialogues.speaker: Zaki
dialogues.text: Hahaha, yes, how considerate of you. Delavar's my friend too, so of course I can take you to him. Come with me.

talks.objective: Go to the place Zaki mentioned

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Are we there yet?

dialogues.speaker: Zaki
dialogues.text: Yep, this is the place.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: This place is practically deserted... What are they doing in a place like this?

dialogues.speaker: Zaki
dialogues.text: Hahaha, why don't you take a guess? Go on, a wild stab in the dark... Hehe, you're like lambs to the slaughter!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, it's an ambush!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: What's all this about, Zaki?

dialogues.speaker: Zaki
dialogues.text: C'mon Dehya, you really think we didn't hear about what you said back in Aaru Village? The boys have kept a close eye on you from the moment you set foot there.

dialogues.speaker: Zaki
dialogues.text: Not only do I know that you're looking for Delavar, I also know that you've teamed up with people from the Akademiya to look for the missing scholars.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: So you've been watching us from the very beginning?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh oh... Paimon knew leaving Cyno behind was a mistake!

dialogues.speaker: Zaki
dialogues.text: Heh, and you left the strongest one in the village, didn't ya? Who do you think you are? You really thought we'd fall for your little "business deal" nonsense?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Tch.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: So you and Delavar have been partners all along.

dialogues.speaker: Zaki
dialogues.text: Hahaha, Dehya, I guess it's only natural for a traveling mercenary like you to be out of the loop. Those of us who hang around the tavern have stronger bonds than you think.

dialogues.speaker: Zaki
dialogues.text: But you got one thing right... We're all looking forward to an uprising in Sumeru. There's nothing more we'd like to see than the desert folk overthrowing the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: If that's the case, then I'm sure Delavar wouldn't miss a second of it.
I'll be honest with you. If it weren't for what you said in the village, your little monologue about the Wall of Samiel would have convinced me that you're one of us.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Delavar... and Engur. You're here, too, huh.

dialogues.speaker: Engur
dialogues.text: Long time no see, Miss Mercenary. You should've known that traitors are what us followers of King Deshret despise the most.

dialogues.speaker: Delavar
dialogues.text: Dehya, I thought that you, a fellow desert-dweller, would understand why King Deshret is greater than the Dendro Archon. Little did I know... you don't deserve to join us.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Yeah, gee, what a missed opportunity... Adopting radical views and kidnapping innocent scholars? All because of some baseless rumors? Anything else I'm missing out on?

dialogues.speaker: Delavar
dialogues.text: See? There you have it... Mercenaries are just a bunch of faithless scum with only one thing on their minds... Mora. Pathetic, you're all like a pack of street rats.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You're not wrong. Mercenaries are driven by Mora, and my faith lies with whoever's paying me. As long as there's a profit to be made, anyone can become my friend.

dialogues.speaker: Zaki
dialogues.text: Enough talking. Get 'em!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hmph, just as I expected. Let's teach 'em a lesson, Traveler!

dialogues.speaker: Zaki
dialogues.text: Impossible! H—How could you...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: So, what do you think about your meticulous network now, Zaki? How did you say it... "It's only natural for a traveling mercenary like me to be out of the loop."

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I'm guessing your informant told you that I'm just an incompetent merc with no real fighting skills, correct? I mean, that is what I said, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: And of course you would believe everything he reported. The only thing you know about me is that I'm a mercenary, but you've never seen me in action.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Even though you heard we went to handle monsters together, you believed that Candace was the only one doing all the real fighting.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: "That so-called Flame-Mane is just a fraud! She admitted it herself: She just uses her connections to gain the trust of others."

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: That's what you thought, right?

dialogues.speaker: Zaki
dialogues.text: Ugh, you lied in the village because you figured that we'd have people watching you...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: And you were stupid enough to fall for it. I figured as much the first time we drank together. You all thought you were so smart. Pathetic.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: With one swift kick, Dehya knocks Zaki unconscious.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Okay, that should be all of 'em.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, so you've been planning this since we were in Aaru Village?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: No task can be done without preparation. I just happened to notice a couple suspicious-looking people while you were out investigating.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... But instead of catching them right away, you let them report back...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Those two who were snooping around were just a couple small fries. If we wanna get the real catch, we have to be patient and give it some time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, those names you mentioned...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean the funny names she mentioned back in Uncle Anpu's house? The Wide-Eyed Butcher, Scar-Riddled Bandit... Uh, Paimon can't remember them all.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: That's just a bunch of drunk talk. Engur and Delavar like to talk themselves up when they're drinking. "Engur the Wide-Eyed Butcher" and "Delavar the Scar-Riddled Bandit" are the nicknames they came up with for themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Alcohol has a way of making people share what they really think, so Engur and Delavar are always rambling in the tavern about how King Deshret is a superior deity.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about Zaki?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: He's just a numbskull who fell right into our trap. Zaki was probably the best hidden of them all. My initial plan was to find Delavar first, and then try to track him down.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So who is the "Ducktail-Bearded Crook"?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: That's what you wanted to ask when we were at Uncle Anpu's house, right? Jabari's one of the villagers you talked to. You know — the one who wanted to treat Isak and his grandpa to some food.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so he's a Radical, too!?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: No, he isn't. I just needed to tack on a random villager name to make the eavesdropper think that I was making some wild guesses based on my impressions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, what a genius idea! Well, that's an expert mercenary for ya!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Ah, you're too kind. It was straight from the usual playbook, if I'm honest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, that thing you were saying before... is it really true?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hmm? About what?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: About how mercenaries only care about Mora, and that anyone's a friend as long as there's a profit...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Does that bother you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't think you're that kind of person.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: What makes you so sure?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Because even without an employer, you're still helping us out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dehya, do you dislike the Dendro Archon like the other desert folk?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Heh, you two are pretty sharp. No, I don't have anything against the Dendro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I've heard a lot of nice things about the Lesser Lord from Dunyarzad. I can understand her devotion and gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Dunyarzad's just an ordinary person. There's no way a god would be so involved in the lives of everyday people unless they were truly compassionate.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I've begun to realize that the sages are behind everything that's happened recently. The Radicals' blind belief in King Deshret, making the Dendro Archon out to be an enemy... It's all the Akademiya's trickery.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: But I see through it all. And unlike them, I could never be hostile towards anyone who's never done anything wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dehya...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Anyway, looks like we're done with business here. Traveler, lend me a hand. Let's tie 'em up and bring 'em to the village.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: This should be all of 'em. I'll let you take it from here.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Alright. I'll be in touch. Until then, please stand by.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Candace, do you need any help?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Candace will be okay on her own. I trust her, so you can too.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: She's been guarding Aaru Village for quite some time now. If anyone is qualified to question the offenders, it's her.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: While I'm questioning them, why don't you pass some time by exploring the area?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I'll meet you back here tomorrow morning, Traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds good.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: As for these idiots... Let's just hope they live to see another day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Dehya!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Right on time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did we learn anything from the criminals?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: We'll know any moment now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's been wondering... You seem to know Candace pretty well. Have you been friends for a long time?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: We've known each other for some time now. She's a pretty interesting person. Even though she's an extremely strong warrior, she never misuses her power against others.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon knows what you mean. Like a lot of martial artists say: "Never take the fight outside the ring."

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Yep, I guess you can put it that way. It takes strong convictions to be as dedicated as she is and shoulder that kind of responsibility.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Us mercs, on the other hand... We pretty much live from one day to the next.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Paimon thinks you're great too!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Really? Thanks for that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Cyno's here! And he's pretty early too!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yes. I was here yesterday to help out a little.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: To help out? By doing what?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Sharing some interrogation techniques.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... You mean, you taught Candace some more... persuasive methods?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Right.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Come on in, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: C'mon, let's go inside.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Candace, we're... Whoa! You look furious!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Do I? Huh... What gave it away?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Oh, there's no mask that can hide true bloodlust. Cover up your eyes and it'll still show itself at the corners of your mouth.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Perhaps I need to work on my composure...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Still, it's perfectly understandable why I'm angry — I'm sure everyone present would agree?

dialogues.speaker: Delavar
dialogues.text: Ah yes, yes M—Ma'am...

dialogues.speaker: Engur
dialogues.text: Please don't beat us anymore... We're gonna die...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, looks like Cyno taught her well...

choices.text: She mastered it really quickly too...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: You fear death yourselves, yet you do not hesitate to place the lives of others at risk. The absurdity is mind-boggling.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: The ones you call "mad scholars" are known to us as "the Village Keepers." They are vital members of our community, and some even count them as family...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: You come here, to my village, and treat my people as nothing more than stepping stones towards your goal... Tell me, what would you do in my position?

response.speaker: Zaki
response.text: Ah! Mercy, please have mercy!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: You've made your bed.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: We may both be desert-dwellers, but there is one thing I understand better than you. The resurrection of King Deshret will only result in war... and war serves no one.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: The people of Aaru Village care little about which god is in power. Life may be tough and tiring, but we wish to preserve our way of life.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: A war would only cause us to lose all that we have, and that is not a responsibility that you can afford to shoulder.

response.speaker: Zaki
response.text: Ah, we understand! We're sorry!

response.speaker: Zaki
response.text: I'll tell you everything I know! Please, just let us go...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: I'm listening.

response.speaker: Zaki
response.text: Uh, you might not believe this, but it wasn't us who came up with this idea. Someone was spreading rumors in the tavern. That's how we ended up hearing about King Deshret's resurrection.

response.speaker: Zaki
response.text: Some mystery man told us that mad scholars will make the perfect sacrifice to usher in King Deshret's resurrection. They give their lives, and we can get anything we wish for.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: They're called Village Keepers. Slip up again and you'll regret it.

response.speaker: Zaki
response.text: Ah, yes, sorry!

response.speaker: Zaki
response.text: It was all that mystery man's doing! He told us to spread the word about King Deshret's resurrection, and talked us into helping him... In return, he said he'll help facilitate the resurrection process.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Where are the Village Keepers now?

response.speaker: Zaki
response.text: I—I'm not sure...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: That's one.

response.speaker: Zaki
response.text: Huh? ...One what?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Strike. You get a total of three, then you die by my hand.

response.speaker: Zaki
response.text: Wait, I'm telling the truth! We don't know anything, it was all him!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Two.

response.speaker: Zaki
response.text: H—He got us to lure them out of their houses in the night with some kind of incense. We take them to a junction outside the village, then the mystery guy takes 'em from there!

response.speaker: Zaki
response.text: You gotta believe me, please! I'm telling the truth, I swear! J—Just ask them if you don't believe me!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: That was indeed the truth. Traveler, go on.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Do you have any idea who that mysterious person might be?

response.speaker: Zaki
response.text: You have to believe me! If I knew that, I woulda told you his name right away! I'm not risking another beating to keep his secrets, no way!

response.speaker: Zaki
response.text: He, um, that guy, he wears a cloak, and he's always careful to cover his face... Uh, he calls himself King Deshret's envoy.

response.speaker: Uncle Anpu
response.text: I believe I may know what's going on.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Uncle Anpu? What do you mean?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Cyno strikes the three crooks unconscious with one swift move.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Heh, smooth!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Okay, speak.

response.speaker: Uncle Anpu
response.text: If my suspicions are correct, this mystery man they speak of could be from the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Uncle Anpu
response.text: Some time ago, people from the Akademiya attempted to take the Village Keepers away. I refused, insisting that they are a part of our community.

response.speaker: Uncle Anpu
response.text: It strikes me now that this secretive character shares the same goal they had.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Which means... it's highly likely that the Akademiya was purposely spreading a false rumor to trick the Radicals into delivering the Village Keepers right into their hands.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Huh, they were the ones who brought them here to begin with... Now they're trying to take them back? We aren't gonna let that happen.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: ...Not the Akademiya again.

choices.text: In Sumeru City, Setaria also mentioned...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Just as I thought.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: But what could they want with the Village Keepers...?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: People are nothing but tools in the eyes of the Akademiya. A change in their plans likely means they've found another way to exploit the scholars.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Regardless, our top priority now is locating the Village Keepers.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: You're right. Isak is still waiting for news on his grandpa...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Time to go. Let's leave the village and try to track them down.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Yes. Pack up and get ready to leave.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: You got it. Candace, I'll let you deal with the Radicals. Leave everything outside the village to us.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Alright.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's meet back here once everyone's ready!

choices.text: King Deshret's resurrection is just the Akademiya's misinformation campaign.
Now she's just as terrifying as he is...

talks.objective: Go back to the village chief's house

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Cyno, please don't take offense. I'm sure Dehya just wants to help everyone solve their problem as quickly as possible. That's why she can be so straightforward at times.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I don't mind.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Ah, I see... Well, from the way you were staring out into the distance, I thought you might have been mulling over Dehya's words.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: No. I'm used to being treated that way.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It's natural to fear strength. I take no objection to it.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: You heard the question. Now answer me.

dialogues.speaker: Delavar
dialogues.text: Arrghh!!!

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: *sigh* Where did Grandpa go... Please come home, Grandpa...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Candace is an expert at dealing with people like this. All we have to do is wait for her word.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Looks like someone has been living in here this entire time...)

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: (These are all daily necessities...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (These footprints are at least rather clear...)

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: (It seems impossible to climb up from here...)
